newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan scraps sugar tender, invites new bids.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan scraps sugar tender, invites new bids.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said on Saturday it had scrapped a tender for 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar and had reinvited bids on December 21 for delivery by January 11.
"The tender has been scrapped," acting TCP chairman Iftikhar Ahmed told Reuters. He said bids had been invited for the same amount to be opened on December 21 at 0500 GMT (1000 local).
TCP tendered on December 7 for the supply of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar for shipment by December 31.
Ahmed said the TCP had received nine bids, including one at $358.50 per tonne c & f.

"Most bids were disqualified as they either did not fulfill our required delivery procedures or were without bid bonds," he said. "Instead of dragging out the whole thing, we have decided to scrap the tender and call for fresh bids."
The tender was issued because of a shortfall due to the delayed start of the cane crushing season in Pakistan.
